subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Three urns have the following composition of balls. Urn I: 1 white, 2 black. Urn II: 2 white, 1 black. Urn III: 2 white, 2 black. One of the urns is selected at random and a ball is drawn. It turns out to be white. Find the probability that it came from urn III.

mark_split.label: Prior probabilities of choosing each container
Probability of the colour from each container

Answer checked: P(W|U₁) = 1/3, P(W|U₂) = 2/3, P(W|U₃) = 2/4 = 1/2; P(W) = (1/3)(1/3 + 2/3 + 1/2) = (1/3)(3/2) = 1/2; P(U₃|W) = (1/6)/(1/2) = 1/3 — agrees with the book.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the probability that the white ball came from urn III — the events, the priors, the three white-ball probabilities, the total, and Bayes.
insider_note: The arithmetic is clean here: 1/3 + 2/3 = 1 makes the bracket 3/2 and the total exactly 1/2. Write every step anyway — the marks are for the method.

steps.label: Define the events
steps.margin_note: First mark. Three urn events and one colour event.
steps.memory_tip: Three urn events and one colour event, including the urns not asked about.

lines.text: Let U₁, U₂, U₃ be the events of selecting
urn I, urn II, urn III respectively, and let
W be the event that the ball drawn is white.

recall.must_convey: That U₁, U₂, U₃ are the events of choosing urns I, II, III and W is the event that the drawn ball is white.
accept: let U one U two U three be choosing the three urns and W be drawing a white ball
define an event for each urn and one for white
U one is urn one and so on, W is white
moodu urns ki U one U two U three, white ball ki W
name the three urn events and the white ball event
heard_as: U one U two U three

steps.why: The urn events are mutually exclusive and exhaustive; W is the observed event. These are the roles Bayes' theorem needs.
common_mistakes: Defining only U₃, the urn asked about.

steps.label: Priors
steps.margin_note: Second mark. One of three urns at random: 1/3 each.
steps.memory_tip: One of three urns at random is 1/3 each, whatever the ball counts are.

lines.text: The urn is chosen at random, so

recall.must_convey: That each urn has probability 1/3 of being chosen.
accept: each urn has probability one third
P of U one equals P U two equals P U three equals one by three
the three priors are all a third
prathi urn ki probability one by three
one urn out of three so a third each

steps.why: Random selection among three urns gives 1/3 each, independent of how many balls each urn holds.
common_mistakes: Weighting the urns by their ball counts (3/10, 3/10, 4/10).
Omitting the priors because they are equal.

steps.label: P(white | each urn)
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Urn I: 1 white of 3. Urn II: 2 white of 3. Urn III: 2 white of 4.
steps.memory_tip: Each over its own urn total: 1 of 3, 2 of 3, 2 of 4. Never 10, the grand total.

accept: white given urn one is one by three, urn two two by three, urn three two by four which is half
the white probabilities are a third, two thirds and a half
P of W given U one is 1 by 3, U two 2 by 3, U three 1 by 2
urn one lo white 1 by 3, urn two lo 2 by 3, urn three lo half
one of three, two of three, two of four

steps.why: Each urn has its own total (3, 3, 4), so each white probability is read inside its own urn.
common_mistakes: Leaving P(W|U₃) as 2/4 and then mis-adding.

steps.label: Total probability of white

accept: P of W is a third times a third plus two thirds plus half which is a third of three by two equals half
total probability of white is one by two
add the three routes, the bracket is three by two, so P W is half
P of white ante one by three into bracket three by two, answer half
the denominator of bayes is one half

steps.why: White can come by three disjoint routes; their probabilities add to give P(W), the denominator of Bayes' theorem.

steps.label: Bayes' theorem
steps.memory_tip: The answer 1/3 equals the prior by coincidence — write the Bayes line anyway.

accept: P of U three given W is a third times half over half which is one third
by bayes theorem the answer is one by three
the urn three route one by six divided by the total half gives a third
bayes prakaram 1 by 6 ni half tho divide cheste one by three
the probability it came from urn three is one third

steps.why: The answer equals the prior 1/3 because P(W|U₃) happens to equal P(W): seeing white gives no new information about urn III in this particular set-up.
common_mistakes: Writing 1/3 without the Bayes line — the number equals the prior by coincidence and the method is not shown.
